text: CHIEF AMENDMENT - THE DOOR COUNT IS ONE, NOT FIVE, established from bytecode with a control. (a) copy DOES NOT EXIST on a private-constructor case class: PopulationAggregate (private ctor) has zero copy methods while SubjectAlignment (public ctor, same module, same compile) has five, so Scala 3 suppresses it and a negative probe for copy tests only that the compiler exists. (b) unapply, _1, _2, productIterator and productElementNames are public but READ-ONLY - they construct nothing and expose only what the public accessors already expose, so closing them buys nothing and costs pattern matching; Product membership is not itself a defect. (c) fromProduct is the ENTIRE defect: the only public member that builds an instance without passing the smart constructor. Each slice therefore closes ONE door and proves ONE property from outside the defining package: the type cannot be built except through its smart constructor. (d) RECORDED CEILING, not a defect and not filed as one: the JVM constructor is PUBLIC in bytecode even for a source-level private constructor - Scala privacy is compiler-enforced, not JVM-enforced - so a Java or Kotlin consumer could call it directly. We ship no Java-facing API, so this changes no priority, but no one may later claim these types are unforgeable from the JVM. The honest ceiling on this sweep is 'sound for Scala consumers'.
